rules: Queries are written from memory of the film, never by reading the TMDB overview -- otherwise the set measures whether the model can match text to a paraphrase of itself.

PREMISE ROWS ONLY for now. Scene queries are parked in queries_scene.json: the corpus describes premises, so scene retrieval is a known failure waiting on corpus enrichment, and mixing the two hides movement in the half that works.
No film appears in more than one row, and no film shares its title with another catalog entry -- a premise query cannot tell an original from its remake, so a row like that would measure label luck.
Phrasing is deliberately how a user types -- lowercase, filler, missing apostrophes -- because that is the real input distribution.
Film titles are never used in the query text; a row that names its own answer measures nothing.
